title: Chorus capacity rail: exploratory dashboard and micro-controls for Dedicated GPU pools
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create an exploratory dashboard concept ("Chorus") that presents GPU pool health as a horizontal 'rail' of compact KPI cards plus embedded micro-controls for autoscale policies and burst allocation. The goal is to enable operators to quickly triage pool health, adjust short-lived burst capacity, and launch canary rollouts for model variants without leaving the pool context. This ticket covers high-fidelity wireframes, an interactive Figma prototype, accessibility considerations, and a short review session with PM and Eng to validate runtime constraints.
background: Operators need a single-pane experience to observe latency/queue/backlog, GPU utilization, prefix cache hit, and cost burn, and then take low-risk actions (small burst, temporary throttle, canary) without deep context switching. Existing console panels are modal-heavy and require multiple pages; Chorus explores inline micro-controls and a 'burst slider' with explicit cost impact preview. Aligns with Dedicated capacity goals (predictable throughput, graceful degradation) and Optimize tooling (cost-awareness).
goals: 1) Surface 4–6 core health metrics per pool in a dense, scannable rail. 2) Provide 3 inline actions: quick-burst (cost preview), autoscale intent toggle (on/off/capped), and canary deploy trigger tied to rollout policy. 3) Ensure actions are reversible and show safety constraints and audit links. 4) Keep keyboard-first navigation and screen-reader compatibility.
acceptance_criteria: High-fidelity Figma frames for desktop width >= 1280px including rail, expanded card, and micro-controls
Interactive prototype demonstrating quick-burst flow with cost preview (k tokens -> $ estimate) and confirmation modal
List of aria patterns and keyboard shortcuts that cover focus order for the rail and inline controls
Design handoff with component spec tokens (colors, spacing, iconography) and interaction states for disabled/confirm/error
PM and Eng sign-off in review notes, plus at least one engineering feasibility note (can/should be implemented without runtime changes)
design_notes:
- Density: Use a single-line rail with collapsible cards; hover/expand reveals history sparkline and last 1h distribution.
- Micro-controls: small primary action (burst) and tertiary 'open rollout' secondary action. Controls should be guarded by two-step confirmations for cost-affecting operations.
- Cost preview: estimate uses recent token burn + configured pricing tier; show quick compare to hourly baseline.
- Safety: burst capped by pool-level policy; if pool is at thermal throttle risk, actions are disabled with inline tooltip pointing to remediation docs.
- Telemetry overlay: toggle to surface anomaly markers (SLO breaches) along the rail.
- Progressive disclosure: minimal visual noise by default; expanded card shows pinned logs, recent rollouts, and a 'why flagged' summary.
- Edge cases: single-GPU pools compress metrics, multi-tenant pools show owner badge and quick-impersonate link.
- Visual language: introduce 'rail' motif (soft rounded container, subtle divider between cards) and an accent color for burst actions to indicate cost impact.
decisions: Use horizontal rail instead of grid to preserve horizontal scanning pattern used by ops teams
Embed micro-controls directly in the rail (vs. contextual flyouts) to reduce clicks for common ops flows
Show cost preview inline rather than in a separate modal: trade-off accepted for speed, confirmation modal still required for commit
Do not allow burst > configured pool cap; engineering to expose cap via API before final handoff
rejected_options: Full-page pool inspector with multi-tab layout (rejected for common triage use as it increases cognitive load)
Auto-apply burst suggestions without confirmation (rejected due to cost and regulatory concerns)
Showing raw GPU telemetry by default (kept to expanded state to avoid noise)
review_feedback: Sofia Martinez (PM): Like the cost-preview concept — ask Eng for a simple pricing API endpoint so we can avoid client-side heuristics.
Noah Kim (Eng): Concern about extra API calls for real-time cost; propose sampling once per 30s and caching results per pool.
Priya Rao (Security): Confirm audit entry for burst actions includes user, pool_id, old_cap, new_cap, and justification field.
Design Review (internal): Increase contrast on burst action color and add a 'safe default' CTA that performs capped burst when user is unsure.
